newsitem.title: USA: PacifiCorp hopes to avoid FERC oversight.
newsitem.headline: PacifiCorp hopes to avoid FERC oversight.

text.p: PacifiCorp is aiming to avoid U.S. Federal Energy Regulatory Comission (FERC) review of its planned acquisition of the U.K.-based Energy Group Plc, company officials said Friday.
"They are breaking a little bit of new ground here, but a FERC review would just take too long," said Ed Tirello, an analyst at NatWest Securities.
The prospect of FERC oversight stems from the fact that both PacifiCorp and Energy Group, through its Citizens Power unit, have FERC-authorized power marketing licenses.
PacifiCorp Chief Financial Officer Dick O'Brien said Friday the combined power marketing operations would be conducted under one license.
"We are not going to take control of Citizen's agreements, since that would put us under FERC jurisdiction," he explained.
Tirello said the company will sell off Citizens' assets, such as the power marketing license and some transmission deals, in order to avoid FERC jurisdiction.
Under U.K. laws, an uncontested acquisition can be completed in 60 to 70 days, he and other analysts said.
FERC, however, is well known for quite lengthy reviews.
"It's pretty difficult to get away from FERC. They tend to get upset when people say we don't need you," said Daniele Seitz, an analyst at UBS Securities.

Previously, utilities such as Pacific Enterprises and Enova Corp have sought to avoid FERC oversight over planned mergers, only to be informed several months later that the agency would invoke jurisdiction.
PacifiCorp said it expects to close the Energy Corp deal by late summer or early fall.
